picks.title: "Our industry is rotting" and AI "pushed things over the edge," so the DayZ creator wants to change how games are made
picks.rationale: A concrete release: Dean Hall launches BRUTAL, a free open-source development framework, with the Kerbal Space Program creator on board, framed as a response to AI. Developers can pick it up directly.
picks.excerpt: Dean Hall says AI pushed the industry over the edge and launches BRUTAL, a free open-source development framework, with the Kerbal Space Program creator on board.

picks.title: Anime Gambling Horror Game Ditches Free Steam Demo So It Doesn't Get Ripped Off By AI
picks.rationale: A studio changed its launch strategy, swapping a public demo for a closed beta, out of fear of genAI clones. Earlier cards covered rip-offs after launch; this one is a defensive release decision indie developers can weigh for themselves.
picks.excerpt: The developers of Drunken Goddess Reflux cancelled their free Steam demo for a closed beta, fearing genAI copycats would clone the game before launch.

picks.title: Masahiro Sakurai says original games will be harder for AI to rip off, but originality also makes them harder to sell
picks.rationale: Sakurai argues that originality is the defense against AI clones, and weighs that against marketability. It pairs naturally with the Drunken Goddess demo decision as design guidance from a top director.
picks.excerpt: Smash Bros and Kirby creator Masahiro Sakurai argues AI has made existing design problems worse, and that originality is the defense against AI clones even if it hurts marketability.

picks.title: Interview: The Video Game Industry's Vibe-Coded Future
picks.rationale: Take-Two's former head of AI and Godot's executive director discuss how vibe coding is flooding game development. It gives practitioners an insider view of the engine and pipeline side of a trend the section has covered only through individual ports and launchers.
picks.excerpt: Take-Two's former head of AI and Godot Engine's executive director discuss the Claude Opus-shaped problem facing game development as vibe coding floods the industry.
